sanskrit: tau rajanyāṃ prabhātāyāṃ snātau hutahutāśanau yathoktam ṛṣiṇā pūrvaṃ tatra tatrābhyagāyatām
english: Those two, at the dawning of the night into day, having bathed and offered oblations into fire as previously instructed by the sage, sang [the poem] here and there [throughout the grounds].

sanskrit: tāṃ sa śuśrāva kākutsthaḥ pūrvacaryāṃ tatas tataḥ apūrvāṃ pāṭhya jātiṃ ca geyena samalaṃkṛtām
english: Kākutstha [Rāma] heard from various places that earlier narrative — a recitation genre unprecedented [in its kind], adorned with melody.

sanskrit: pramāṇair bahubhir baddhāṃ tantrīlayasamanvitām bālābhyāṃ rāghavaḥ śrutvā kautūhalaparo 'bhavat
english: Hearing it composed in many metres and accompanied by the rhythm of the lute, Rāghava [Rāma] became wholly absorbed in wonder.

sanskrit: atha karmāntare rājā samānīya mahāmunīn pārthivāṃś ca naravyāghraḥ paṇḍitān naigamāṃs tathā
english: Then, in a pause between ritual acts, the king — that tiger among men — assembled the great sages, the kings, the learned scholars, and the Vedic experts,

sanskrit: paurāṇikāñ śabdavito ye ca vṛddhā dvijātayaḥ etān sarvān samānīya gātārau samaveśayat
english: the Purāṇa specialists, the grammarians, and the elder twice-born — having gathered all of them together, he had the two singers take their seats [before the assembly].

sanskrit: hṛṣṭā ṛṣigaṇās tatra pārthivāś ca mahaujasaḥ pibanta iva cakṣurbhyāṃ rājānaṃ gāyakau ca tau
english: The groups of sages there, and the kings of great splendour, were filled with delight — drinking in, as it were, with their eyes both the king and those two singers.

sanskrit: parasparam athocus te sarva eva samaṃ tataḥ ubhau rāmasya sadṛśau bimbād bimbam ivoddhṛtau
english: Then all of them spoke to one another at once: "Both of these resemble Rāma — as if one image were drawn from another image."

sanskrit: jaṭilau yadi na syātāṃ na valkaladharau yadi viśeṣaṃ nādhigacchāmo gāyato rāghavasya ca
english: "Were they not wearing matted locks, were they not clad in bark garments, we could find no difference between these two singers and Rāghava [himself]."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃvadatām evaṃ śrotṝṇāṃ harṣavardhanam geyaṃ pracakratus tatra tāv ubhau munidārakau
english: While the listeners conversed in this way, growing in joy, those two sons of the sage commenced their song there, increasing [the audience's] delight.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravṛttaṃ madhuraṃ gāndharvam atimānuṣam na ca tṛptiṃ yayuḥ sarve śrotāro geya saṃpadā
english: Then there arose a sweet celestial music surpassing the human — and none of the listeners reached satiation with the wealth of that song.

sanskrit: pravṛttam āditaḥ pūrvaṃ sargān nāradadarśanāt tataḥ prabhṛti sargāṃś ca yāvadviṃśaty agāyatām
english: Beginning from the very beginning — from the cantos opened by the vision of Nārada — they sang forward from there, up to twenty cantos.

sanskrit: tato 'parāhṇasamaye rāghavaḥ samabhāṣata śrutvā viṃśatisargāṃs tān bharataṃ bhrātṛvatsalaḥ
english: Then in the late afternoon, having heard those twenty cantos, Rāghava — who was affectionate toward his brothers — spoke to Bharata:

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśa sahasrāṇi suvarṇasya mahātmanoḥ dadasva śīghraṃ kākutstha bālayor mā vṛthā śramaḥ
english: "Give quickly eighteen thousand [coins] of gold to these two noble souls, O Kākutstha — let the effort of these boys not go unrewarded."

sanskrit: dīyamānaṃ suvarṇaṃ tan nāgṛhṇītāṃ kuśīlavau ūcatuś ca mahātmānau kim aneneti vismitau
english: But those two bards [Kuśa and Lava] did not accept the gold being offered, and the noble-souled pair spoke in astonishment: "What is this to us?"

sanskrit: vanyena phalamūlena niratu svo vanaukasau suvarṇena hiraṇyena kiṃ kariṣyāvahe vane
english: "We are forest-dwellers fully content with wild fruits and roots. What use have we for gold or precious metal in the forest?"

sanskrit: tathā tayoḥ prabruvatoḥ kautūhalasamanvitāḥ śrotāraś caiva rāmaś ca sarva eva suvismitāḥ
english: As the two spoke thus, the listeners and Rāma alike — all of them — filled with curiosity and were greatly astonished.

sanskrit: tasya caivāgamaṃ rāmaḥ kāvyasya śrotum utsukaḥ papraccha tau mahātejās tāv ubhau munidārakau
english: And Rāma, the greatly resplendent, eager to hear the full extent of that poem, asked those two sons of the sage:

sanskrit: kiṃpramāṇam idaṃ kāvyaṃ kā pratiṣṭhā mahātmanaḥ kartā kāvyasya mahataḥ ko vāsau munipuṃgavaḥ
english: "What is the measure of this poem? What is the foundation [topic] of this great noble work? Who is he — that foremost sage who is the author of this great poem?"

sanskrit: pṛcchantaṃ rāghavaṃ vākyam ūcatur munidārakau vālmīkir bhagavān kartā saṃprāpto yajñasaṃnidhim yenedaṃ caritaṃ tubhyam aśeṣaṃ saṃpradarśitam
english: The two sons of the sage replied to Rāghava's questioning words: "The venerable Vālmīki is the author — he who has come to be near the sacrifice — and it is he who has revealed this entire story to you in full."

sanskrit: ādiprabhṛti rājendra pañcasarga śatāni ca pratiṣṭhā jīvitaṃ yāvat tāvad rājañ śubhāśubham
english: "From the very beginning, O lord of kings, [it extends through] five hundred cantos. Its subject, O king, is whatever is auspicious and inauspicious throughout [your] life."

sanskrit: yadi buddhiḥ kṛtā rājañ śravaṇāya mahāratha karmāntare kṣaṇī hūtas tac chṛṇuṣva sahānujaḥ
english: "If your mind is resolved to hear [it], O king, O great warrior — being called to a moment's pause between ritual acts — then listen to it together with your younger brothers."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity abravīd rāmas tau cānujñāpya rāghavam prahṛṣṭau jagmatur vāsaṃ yatrāsau munipuṃgavaḥ
english: Rāma said "So be it," and those two, having received permission from Rāghava, went joyfully to the dwelling where that foremost sage resided.

sanskrit: rāmo 'pi munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ pārthivaiś ca mahātmabhiḥ śrutvā tad gītamādhuryaṃ karmaśālām upāgamat
english: And Rāma too, having savoured the sweetness of that song, returned to the ritual hall together with the sages and the great-souled kings.

sanskrit: rāmo bahūny ahāny eva tad gītaṃ paramādbhutam śuśrāva munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ rājabhiḥ saha vānaraiḥ
english: For many days together Rāma listened to that supremely wondrous song — in the company of the sages, the kings, and the monkeys.

sanskrit: tasmin gīte tu vijñāya sītāputrau kuśīlavau tasyāḥ pariṣado madhye rāmo vacanam abravīt
english: Then, recognising Kuśa and Lava as Sītā's sons from that song, Rāma spoke words in the midst of that assembly:

sanskrit: madvaco brūta gacchadhvam iti bhagavato 'ntikam
english: "Convey my words and go into the presence of the venerable [Vālmīki]:"

sanskrit: yadi śuddhasamācārā yadi vā vītakalmaṣā karotv ihātmanaḥ śuddhim anumānya mahāmunim
english: "'If [Sītā] is pure in conduct, if she is indeed free of all stain, let her establish her own purity here, having gained the great sage's sanction.'"

sanskrit: chandaṃ munes tu vijñāya sītāyāś ca manogatam pratyayaṃ dātukāmāyās tataḥ śaṃsata me laghu
english: "'Having ascertained the sage's pleasure and the inner intent of Sītā — who is willing to give proof — then report to me promptly.'"

sanskrit: śvaḥ prabhāte tu śapathaṃ maithilī janakātmajā karotu pariṣanmadhye śodhanārthaṃ mameha ca
english: "'Tomorrow morning, let Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, take her oath in the midst of the assembly — for the purpose of [her] vindication and of mine here as well.'"

sanskrit: śrutvā tu rāghavasyaitad vacaḥ paramam adbhutam dūtāḥ saṃprayayur vāṭaṃ yatrāste munipuṃgavaḥ
english: Having heard this supremely wondrous speech of Rāghava, the messengers hastened to the grove where that foremost sage dwelt.

sanskrit: te praṇamya mahātmānaṃ jvalantam amitaprabham ūcus te rāma vākyāni mṛdūni madhurāṇi ca
english: They bowed before the great-souled one blazing with boundless radiance and spoke to him Rāma's words — gentle and sweet.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā rāmasya ca manogatam vijñāya sumahātejā munir vākyam athābravīt
english: Having heard their report and understood the inner intention of Rāma, the sage of very great splendour then spoke:

sanskrit: evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ vo yathā tuṣyati rāghavaḥ tathā kariṣyate sītā daivataṃ hi patiḥ striyāḥ
english: "May it be so — blessings upon you. As Rāghava wishes, so shall Sītā act; for the husband is the deity of a woman."

sanskrit: tathoktā muninā sarve rāmadūtā mahaujasaḥ pratyetya rāghavaṃ sarve munivākyaṃ babhāṣire
english: Thus addressed by the sage, all of Rāma's messengers — those of great strength — returned and reported the sage's words to Rāghava.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ kākutsthaḥ śrutvā vākyaṃ mahātmanaḥ ṛṣīṃs tatra sametāṃś ca rājñaś caivābhyabhāṣata
english: Then Kākutstha, greatly delighted upon hearing the words of the great-souled sage, addressed the sages assembled there and the kings as well:

sanskrit: bhagavantaḥ saśiṣyā vai sānugaś ca narādhipāḥ paśyantu sītāśapathaṃ yaś caivānyo 'bhikāṅkṣate
english: "Let the venerable sages together with their disciples, and the lords of men with their retinues, witness the oath of Sītā — and whoever else desires to.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ sarveṣam ṛṣimukhyānāṃ sādhuvādo mahān abhūt
english: On hearing those words of the great-souled Rāghava, there arose a great cry of "bravo!" from all the foremost sages.

sanskrit: rājānaś ca mahātmānaḥ praśaṃsanti sma rāghavam upapannaṃ naraśreṣṭha tvayy eva bhuvi nānyataḥ
english: The great-souled kings too praised Rāghava: "This befits you alone, O best of men — nowhere else on earth."

sanskrit: evaṃ viniścayaṃ kṛtvā śvobhūta iti rāghavaḥ visarjayām āsa tadā sarvāṃs tāñ śatrusūdanaḥ
english: Having thus made this decision — "It shall be tomorrow" — Rāghava, the slayer of enemies, then dismissed all of them.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ rajanyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ yajñavāṭagato nṛpaḥ ṛṣīn sarvān mahātejāḥ śabdāpayati rāghavaḥ
english: When that night had passed, the king Rāghava — greatly resplendent — having gone to the sacrificial arena, summoned all the sages.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho vāmadevaś ca jābālir atha kāśyapaḥ viśvāmitro dīrghatapā durvāsāś ca mahātapāḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Jābāli, and then Kāśyapa; Viśvāmitra of long austerities, and Durvāsas of great ascetic power;

sanskrit: agastyo 'tha tathāśaktir bhārgavaś caiva vāmanaḥ mārkaṇḍeyaś ca dīrghāyur maudgalyaś ca mahātapāḥ
english: Agastya, and likewise Āśakti, the Bhārgava Vāmana, Mārkaṇḍeya of long life, and Maudgalya of great austerities;

sanskrit: bhārgavaś cyavanaś caiva śatānandaś ca dharmavit bharadvājaś ca tejasvī agniputraś ca suprabhaḥ
english: The Bhārgava Cyavana, Śatānanda who is learned in dharma, the radiant Bharadvāja, and Agniputra of great lustre —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca munayo bahavaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ rājānaś ca naravyāghrāḥ sarva eva samāgatāḥ
english: these and many other sages of sharpened vows, and kings — those tigers among men — all assembled together.

sanskrit: rākṣasāś ca mahāvīryā vānarāś ca mahābalāḥ samājagmur mahātmānaḥ sarva eva kutūhalāt
english: Rākṣasas of great valour and monkeys of great strength — all those noble souls — came together out of eager curiosity.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāś caiva vaiśyāś ca śūdrāś caiva sahasraśaḥ sītāśapathavīkṣārthaṃ sarva eva samāgatāḥ
english: Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras by the thousands — all of them assembled together for the purpose of witnessing Sītā's oath.

sanskrit: tathā samāgataṃ sarvam aśvabhūtam ivācalam śrutvā munivaras tūrṇaṃ sasītaḥ samupāgamat
english: Hearing that all had thus assembled — still as a motionless mountain — the foremost sage quickly approached together with Sītā.

sanskrit: tam ṛṣiṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ sītā sānvagacchad avāṅmukhī kṛtāñjalir bāṣpagalā kṛtvā rāmaṃ manogatam
english: Sītā followed behind that sage with downcast face, hands folded in reverence, tears flowing, having placed Rāma in her heart.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā śrīm ivāyāntīṃ brahmāṇam anugāminīm vālmīkeḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ sītāṃ sādhukāro mahān abhūt
english: Seeing Sītā approaching behind Vālmīki like Śrī following Brahmā, there arose a great acclamation [from the assembly].

sanskrit: tato halahalā śabdaḥ sarveṣām evam ābabhau duḥkhajena viśālena śokenākulitātmanām
english: Then a tumultuous clamour arose from all — those whose hearts were agitated by a vast grief born of sorrow [for her].

sanskrit: sādhu sīteti ke cit tu sādhu rāmeti cāpare ubhāv eva tu tatrānye sādhu sādhv iti cābruvan
english: Some cried "Well done, Sītā!", others cried "Well done, Rāma!" — while yet others there said "Well done, well done!" [meaning both].

sanskrit: tato madhyaṃ janaughānāṃ praviśya munipuṃgavaḥ sītāsahāyo vālmīkir iti hovāca rāghavam
english: Then, entering the midst of the throng of people, that foremost sage Vālmīki — with Sītā beside him — thus spoke to Rāghava:

sanskrit: iyaṃ dāśarathe sītā suvratā dharmacāriṇī apāpā te parityaktā mamāśramasamīpataḥ
english: "O son of Daśaratha, this Sītā — of excellent vows and virtuous conduct — sinless, was abandoned by you near my hermitage.

sanskrit: lokāpavādabhītasya tava rāma mahāvrata pratyayaṃ dāsyate sītā tām anujñātum arhasi
english: "O Rāma, O upholder of great vows — out of fear of public censure you [cast her out]; Sītā shall now give proof [of her purity]. You should grant her permission to do so.

sanskrit: imau ca jānakī putrāv ubhau ca yamajātakau sutau tavaiva durdharṣo satyam etad bravīmi te
english: "These two sons of Jānakī, born as twins — they are your sons indeed, O unconquerable one. I speak this truth to you.

sanskrit: pracetaso 'haṃ daśamaḥ putro rāghavanandana na smarāmy anṛtaṃ vākyaṃ tathemau tava putrakau
english: "I am the tenth son of Pracetas [Varuṇa], O joy of the Rāghava clan — I do not recall ever speaking a falsehood; and likewise, these two are your sons.

sanskrit: bahuvarṣasahasrāṇi tapaścaryā mayā kṛtā tasyāḥ phalam upāśnīyām apāpā maithilī yathā
english: "For many thousands of years I have performed austerities — may I reap the fruit of that [penance] insofar as Maithilī is sinless.

sanskrit: ahaṃ pañcasu bhūteṣu manaḥṣaṣṭheṣu rāghava vicintya sītāṃ śuddheti nyagṛhṇāṃ vananirjhare
english: "Having contemplated, O Rāghava, through [my knowledge of] the five elements together with the mind as sixth, that Sītā is pure — it was thus that I took her in at the forest stream.

sanskrit: iyaṃ śuddhasamācārā apāpā patidevatā lokāpavādabhītasya dāsyati pratyayaṃ tava
english: "This woman of pure conduct, sinless, who holds her husband as her deity — she shall give you proof, who feared the censure of the world."
